btcpay.title: BTCPay connection
btcpay.description: OpenSplit reads settled invoices and sends split payouts through your own BTCPay Server. Nothing is custodied here.
btcpay.setupCtaBody: Save your BTCPay server URL, create an API key with the minimal permissions using the button below, then paste the key and your store ID here.
btcpay.urlError: Enter a full URL — https://btcpay.example.com, http://localhost:3003, or http://host.docker.internal:3003
btcpay.urlHintDocker: Server-side address; links open via {{hostname}} in your browser.
btcpay.urlHint: The address OpenSplit’s server uses to reach BTCPay — must start with http:// or https://
btcpay.storeIdHint: Copy it from your BTCPay store settings.
btcpay.apiKeyHintReplace: Greenfield API key — the stored value is never shown. Enter a new key to replace it.
btcpay.apiKeyHint: Greenfield API key — the stored value is never shown.
btcpay.openBtcpay: Open BTCPay to create an API key
btcpay.saveAllFirst: Save the server URL, store ID, and API key first
btcpay.testError: Could not run the connection test
btcpay.authorizeError: Save the BTCPay server URL first
btcpay.unlockHint: The API-key button unlocks once the server URL is saved.
btcpay.unsavedChanges: Unsaved changes — Test connection runs against the last saved values, so save your changes first (or discard them).
btcpay.stale: Stale — settings changed after this test ran

webhook.title: Webhook
webhook.description: BTCPay pushes settled invoices to OpenSplit through a signed webhook. Events without a valid signature are rejected.
webhook.setupCtaBody: Splits only run once BTCPay can deliver signed events. Generate a secret here, then create the webhook in BTCPay with it — the guided steps appear after generating.
webhook.createSteps: Create the webhook in BTCPay (Store settings → Webhooks → Create Webhook):
webhook.step1: Paste this as the Payload URL
webhook.localHint: This is the address BTCPay must reach — it is served from BTCPay's own network, not your browser.
webhook.shownOnce: Shown only once — paste it into BTCPay now.
webhook.step3: Under events, choose “Send specific events” and tick:
webhook.done: Done — I saved it in BTCPay
webhook.updateSecretWarning: Update the secret in BTCPay — old events will be rejected.
webhook.generateError: Could not generate the webhook secret
webhook.regenerateDescription: The current secret stops working immediately. BTCPay keeps signing with the old one until you paste the new secret there, so deliveries will be rejected in the meantime.
